title: H2 file-list items must be markdown links

spec.name: llms.txt (llmstxt.org)
spec.normative_quote: Zero or more markdown sections delimited by H2 headers, containing "file lists" of URLs where further detail is available... Each "file list" is a markdown list, containing a required markdown hyperlink [name](url), then optionally a : and notes about the file.
spec.note: conformance_testable is false -- llmstxt.org itself is descriptive/indexing, not conformance-tested. Verified against the pinned source (AnswerDotAI/llms-txt @c7178b9, nbs/index.qmd) on 2026-07-30. The quote joins two SEPARATE Format list items -- the parent H2 bullet (source line 45) and its nested child (line 46) -- with an ellipsis; neither is reworded. Source line 45 ends "...is available" with no period; backticks around [name](url) and : are de-marked. Corrects two defects: an earlier version invented a SHOULD and dropped the term "file lists"; this review pass removed a fabricated period that had spliced the two items into continuous prose (the same splice defect security-txt-expires-missing's note describes).

applicability: An H2 section's list item (a line matching /^[-*]\s+/) once at least one H2 has been seen -- AND ONLY IN A BODY WITH A VALID H1. validate-llms-txt.mjs:61 returns immediately when the first non-blank line is not an H1 ('structure is unrecoverable past this point'), so this rule never runs on an H1-less body however many H2 sections it contains. Added by the ADR 0036 Posture-3 rehearsal, which found this precondition unstated here and in llms-txt-h2-no-file-list; it is the same omission ADR 0011's security.txt rehearsal found and fixed on that one rule only (cases/h2-under-missing-h1.txt below pins it).
expectation: The list item matches /^[-*]\s+\[name\]\(url\)(: notes)?$/, where the optional tail is a colon followed by ANY text INCLUDING NOTHING -- the implementing regex is /(:\s*.*)?$/, so '- [Name](url):' with an empty tail is legal. Stated explicitly because the ADR 0036 rehearsal read '(: notes)?' as requiring notes, which diverged on 60 of 20,000 fuzz inputs while passing every case then declared. The permissive tail is recorded as the implementation's behaviour, not endorsed: tightening it to require notes is a candidate change, and would need this line and cases/link-item-bare-colon.txt to move together.

cases.name: a link item with a bare trailing colon and no notes is legal (ADR 0036: pins the permissive tail)
a bare-URL list item, not a markdown link
